label: Person
name: Nectanebo I
summary:
Nectanebo I was the last pharaoh of the 30th Dynasty of Ancient Egypt, ruling from approximately 390 to 361 BCE. Born into a period of great upheaval following the death of Ramses III and the subsequent loss of Egyptian territories to the Persians.

This marked a pivotal moment in Egyptian history as Nectanebo I attempted to restore Egypt's former glory by reviving its military might, economic prosperity, and cultural achievements. Despite initial successes, his efforts were ultimately unsuccessful against the growing Persian Empire, which had already conquered Lydia and Babylon.

The legacy of Nectanebo I lies in his unwavering dedication to Egyptian traditions and his attempts to preserve the country's independence in the face of overwhelming external pressure. His reign also saw significant architectural achievements, including the construction of temples and monuments throughout Egypt.

In the end, it was the Persians who ultimately prevailed, incorporating Egypt into their vast empire and bringing an end to Nectanebo I's reign. Yet, his actions served as a testament to the enduring spirit of Ancient Egyptian resistance against foreign occupation.

'Egypt will be restored,' he declared, a phrase that would become synonymous with the aspirations of future generations.
